chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Wasiti from Qasim al-Sayqal said:

I wrote to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'I make sword sheaths from the skins of dead donkeys, so they touch my clothes; should I pray in them?' He wrote to me: 'Take a specific garment for your prayer.'

Then I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I wrote to your father (peace be upon him) such and such, and he made it difficult for me regarding that, so I started making them from the skins of wild donkeys that were slaughtered.'
He wrote to me: 'All acts of righteousness are with patience, may Allah have mercy on you. If it is from what you make, wild and slaughtered, then there is no harm.'

key_terms.اَلْحُمُرِ اَلْمَيْتَةِ: Dead donkeys (specifically referring to their skins)

ai.seo_question: Is clothing that touches dead donkey skin impure for prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the practical application of fiqh principles regarding the purity of leather from animals not slaughtered according to Islamic rites, specifically contrasting the views of Imam al-Rida and his father Imam al-Jawad. It highlights the scholarly nuance between strict precaution (taking a separate garment) and leniency based on the animal's status as 'wild' and 'slaughtered,' reflecting the dynamic nature of Shia legal reasoning. The narrative underscores the importance of seeking clarification from the Imams on specific occupational details that affect ritual validity.
